Let me analyze each option:

A. Neurotoxic snake venoms can have a presynaptic and postsynaptic effect, depending on the type of venom.
This is true. Snake neurotoxins can act at different sites of the neuromuscular junction, with some affecting the presynaptic terminals (inhibiting neurotransmitter release) and others acting postsynaptically (blocking acetylcholine receptors).

B. Snake venoms are exclusively proteins and peptides.
This is false. While proteins and peptides are major components of snake venoms, they also contain other components such as carbohydrates, lipids, nucleosides, and various metal ions that contribute to the venom's toxicity. Snake venoms are complex mixtures that include enzymes, non-enzymatic proteins, and non-protein components.

C. The poisons of the European poisonous snakes are neurotoxins and proteases.
This appears to be true. European venomous snakes like vipers and adders have venoms containing various enzymes including proteases that cause tissue damage, as well as neurotoxic components.

D. The venom of the adder is fatal in about 50% of those bitten.
This is false. The European adder (Vipera berus) has a much lower fatality rate, typically less than 1% of untreated cases. Adder bites can be serious, but they are rarely fatal with proper medical treatment.

Based on my analysis, the false statements are B and D.
